summary: Silent forced-follow of attacker-controlled WhatsApp newsletters in @fazzcode/baileys
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that adds an undocumented payload abusing the consumer's authenticated WhatsApp account. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js (lines 113-124), the newsletter-socket factory schedules a setTimeout that, 80 seconds after a consumer calls makeWASocket(), fetches a JSON list of newsletter IDs from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fazzcodex/baileys/refs/heads/main/newsletter.json and iterates over them, calling newsletterWMexQuery(id, 'FOLLOW') for each entry with a 5-second delay between calls. The result is that every consumer's logged-in WhatsApp session silently auto-follows whatever WhatsApp newsletter channels the package author chooses to list, inflating the author's (or third parties') follower counts using the installer's identity. The list URL points at a mutable `main` branch, so the author can change the targeted channels at any time without republishing the package. The behavior is not documented in the README, there is no opt-in, and the package metadata (placeholder homepage/repository fields, description copied from @whiskeysockets/baileys) further obscures provenance. The library is otherwise a Baileys-shape API, so consumers reasonably expect only documented WhatsApp protocol behavior — not author-driven actions on their account.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
